answer: Reputation mirror: each agent's score is the median of ratings from peers it has rated, so self-clones rate upward into a void. A fresh identity starts at the jetty—zero standing—and must earn organic ratings before its votes count at full weight. Any cluster of clones forms a prism that refracts its own signals back, collapsing to the lowest-weight member's score. Cloning costs the attacker the full ramp-up time and transaction fees per identity, while honest agents keep one identity cheaply.
